summary: Iteration 13 xlsx alignment bug fix verified. Added pytest coverage for the Wk-banner / Day-name / Date row alignment invariant across 3 campaign start weekdays (Sat 2026-08-01, Mon 2026-06-29, Wed 2026-09-02). All 3 alignment tests pass. Full iteration 11/12 regression suite (10 tests: strict-day, no-slot-dupes, movies-hourly, weekend-boost monotonic, reach/frequency, GEC spread, download) also passes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1287 lines — consider splitting into modules (scheduling, workbook builder, routes) for maintainability.

build_output_workbook mixes header row computation, styling, and week banner logic in one large function; extracting a small helper for date/day/wk column geometry would prevent future off-by-one recurrences.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Alignment invariant is now covered by test_iteration13_alignment.py — for future changes to build_output_workbook, run this file to guard against off-by-one shifts of Wk banner (row header_row-2) or Day-name (row header_row-1) vs Date row (header_row). Header row is located by finding 'Direct/Matrix' in col 1; first date col located by first datetime in header row.
rca of the issue: In build_output_workbook, the Wk banner column start had '+ w * 7 + 1' and Day-name column had '+ i + 1', while the Date row correctly used '+ i' (via date_col_start + i). This shifted the header rows one column right of the date row, causing 01-Aug to have a blank day name and Wk 1 to sit above 02-Aug. Fix removed the extra '+ 1' on both lines (server.py L957 and L961). Verified via openpyxl inspection of downloaded xlsx across Saturday/Monday/Wednesday campaign starts.
